passage: Sunday night. Vasudha, my junior, missed three weekly tasks in a row. As the mentor I was about to feel irritated, then decided to ask instead. Over tea Vasudha said quietly, "The plan clashes with my exams. I'm sorry, I didn't know how to say it." I felt a little ashamed, because I had made the plan in September and never looked at the exam calendar. So we cut it down: for the next two weeks, one small exercise instead of three, and the Saturday review moves to fifteen minutes. We'll return to the full plan after exams. Vasudha looked lighter. Lesson for me: low progress can be a sign that my plan is wrong, not that the junior is lazy. Vaibhav

qa.a: Vasudha probably feels relieved and safer speaking up, since the reason was heard and the plan was lightened.

passage:
In the small college in Bagalkot, Jahnavi had been mentoring Tejas in spoken English and interview skills since June. Every week she gave him two things: a short article to read aloud and five practice questions to answer in writing.
In August he stopped doing them. Three weeks in a row, the notebook came back blank. Jahnavi felt a flicker of irritation, then decided to ask instead of assuming.
'Tejas, what's happening? No blame.'
He looked at the floor. 'Harvest season, akka. I'm in the fields with my father from six till college, and after college till dark. And the semester exams start in two weeks.'
Jahnavi hadn't known about the harvest at all. 'Okay. For the next two weeks, forget the articles. Just one practice question each week, and you can answer it aloud to me after class instead of writing.'
Tejas let out a breath. 'That I can do.'
After exams and harvest, the notebook started filling up again.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi give Tejas every week?
qa.a: A short article to read aloud and five practice questions to answer in writing.

qa.q: How did Jahnavi feel when the notebook came back blank, and what did she choose?
qa.a: She felt a flicker of irritation, but chose to ask why instead of assuming.

qa.q: What could Jahnavi do to avoid a similar clash next year?
qa.a: Ask Tejas at the start about harvest and exam times, and plan lighter weeks around them.

qa.q: How does the lighter plan feel to Tejas?
qa.a: Tejas feels relieved, letting out a breath, since one spoken question fits his harvest days.

grounding: Shows a mentor noticing missed tasks, asking why, learning of harvest work and exams, and lightening the plan for two weeks.
